With AUTO_PREFETCH an active superuser skips the prefetch, and on a cache miss every permission of the object's type is queried and cached before the empty-list early exit can apply.

labels.rationale: With prompt=none and forced approval the view now looks up prior authorizations: one covering the requested scopes, claims and resources produces the authorization response, and when consent is still needed it redirects with consent_required.
The method now accepts an error argument that used to raise TypeError and puts its value in the redirect, so a caller can signal consent_required; omitting it still gives login_required.
New helper deciding whether a token's RFC 8707 resources cover the requested ones.

DENIED now takes precedence; for a pending or authorized device past its deadline, is_expired() saves the EXPIRED status and the view returns expired_token, which ends the polling without issuing a token.

The import gives an oauthlib exception the name OAuthlibFatalClientError; form_valid catches it and decides the response, labeled on its own.

On denied consent the method now validates the client and writes the resolved URI, possibly the default one, into the caller's credentials dict, and raises a fatal error without the rejected URI when validation fails.

A new method, empty by the rule for added symbols; validating the URI is labeled on the two methods that start calling it.

labels.rationale: The transaction now calls the module-level function to pack MULTI, the commands and EXEC; the usual packing is equivalent, but a subclass that overrides _pack_commands no longer takes part in that call.
The pipeline sends its setup and queued commands to the module-level packer, keeping the usual packing but no longer dispatching to an override of _pack_commands on the instance or a subclass.
The method is removed from Pipeline: a caller that awaited pipeline._pack_commands(...) loses that way to get the bytes, though the two internal callers moved to the equivalent module function.
New module-level helper holding the former Pipeline._pack_commands logic.
The 1000-command threshold applies here too: with 999 commands the node packs on the event loop thread, from 1000 it hands packing to another thread, and other tasks can run before the write.

The 1000-command threshold counts MULTI and EXEC: 997 ordinary commands are packed on the event loop thread, while 998 reach it and are handed to another thread, so other tasks can run before the send.
The module imports the packer from redis.asyncio.client, which it already imported classes from; the decision to hand packing to another thread is made when a batch is packed.

labels.rationale: With decode_responses on, NEVER_DECODE now asks the executor to return the binary chunk as bytes, which also avoids the decoding error a chunk that does not fit the client's encoding could raise.
Two distinct ranges longer than sys.maxsize can now be compared: reading _len removes the limit len() imposed, so True or False comes back where OverflowError could be raised.
A range of more than sys.maxsize items can now be a dict key: the hash reads the internal length and returns an integer where len() raised OverflowError.

When iteration starts, n=0 now yields no chunks and a negative n raises its own ValueError before the iterator is taken, where the old code could consume items filling its buffer and only then fail in islice.

The call now returns a filter object and builds zip_longest right away, so an __iter__ with effects runs at the call and a non-iterable argument raises TypeError there; items are still read on demand.

For p[5::-1] only the first six items are now cached, which changes the read limit, the cache contents and the calls to the iterator; the slice ends even on an infinite source and avoids errors the source could raise further on.
Only the __version__ string changes, from 11.2.0 to 11.2.1.
Only the __version__ string changes, from 11.1.0 to 11.2.0; the changes to tail and iter_index are labeled on their own.

With n=-1 and a list, tail now reads its length and returns an iterator that consumes the input without yielding values, while deque rejects the size for a source without a length; both calls failed before touching the input.

With a negative bound and a source without an index method, the whole source used to be consumed into a tuple and searched; islice now rejects the bound with ValueError when the search starts, consuming no items and yielding none of the earlier indices.
